Hi Abby — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear constraints.

I put together an initial, one-page tier overview and a practical procurement path for Clearline. High level (details attached in the tier sheet):

- Starter: annual commit 10M tokens, 15% list discount, includes 10% onboarding credit, basic SLA (99.9%). Good for pilots and early production.
- Growth: annual commit 120M tokens (monthly pathed), 25% list discount, 15% onboarding, 24/7 support, burst pool for 2x committed throughput for short periods.
- Enterprise: annual commit 600M+ tokens, custom pricing (typically 30–40% off list depending on term), prioritized capacity, custom SLAs, dedicated account engineering.

Overage handling options:
- Metered overage at committed price + 10% for Starter; for Growth/Enterprise overage can be blended into month-to-month true-ups or converted to short-term burst credits.

Smoothing alternatives for CFO: quarterly invoicing with carryover credits, or fixed monthly billing with a year-end reconciliation (common for customers with predictable ramps).

I attached the Redwood_Annual_Tier_Sheet_v2.xlsx and a small procurement checklist. Marissa will follow up with numbers and a recommended path that matches your ramp. Neha included technical notes about burst and quota. Laura will propose onboarding milestones tied to success metrics.

If Thursday EOD is the ask, we can deliver a short version + procurement checklist by then and a full packet by next Monday.

Best,
Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Abby — following up with the concrete numbers you can hand to procurement. See attached pricing sheet. Key recommendation for Clearline given your ramp: start on Growth with a 12-month front-loaded ramp (10M -> 30M -> steady 30M), with an auto-burst allowance and a smoothing clause.

Quick summary (net to Clearline after standard negotiation anchors):
- Starter: 10M / year, $0.015/token list -> net $0.0128/token (15% off). Low administrative friction.
- Growth: 120M / year (pathed), $0.010/token list -> net $0.0075/token (25% off) with 10% advanced credit for onboarding and 2 months carryover credit window.
- Enterprise: 600M+ / year -> custom net in $0.005–0.007 range with SLA credits and dedicated throughput lanes.

Procurement notes:
- We normally include a "flex credit" clause: unspent committed tokens convert to credits usable for the next 90 days or for one-time extra throughput. This eases CFOs worried about strict use-it-or-lose-it.
- For pilot: propose a 3-month refundable onboarding credit ($X) tied to defined KPIs.

I also attached a short doc with suggested contract redlines we typically accept (payment terms, refund mechanics, audit language).

1) Jonas/Marissa: finalize the tier sheet and legal-friendly clause language by Thu EOD.
2) Abby: confirm whether procurement requires PO-first vs. DocuSign signature.
3) Neha/Laura: we’ll add a technical appendix for burst behavior and onboarding milestones.

Thanks — I’ll be available on Thursday for a 30-min call if useful.

Abby — quick technical clarifications to include in the appendix so procurement gets the right expectations:

- Burst behavior: bursts are provided from a shared pool for Growth customers up to 2x committed throughput sustained for 15 minutes; Enterprise can get dedicated burst lanes with longer sustained windows. Bursts are subject to global capacity and regional availability.
- KV/prefix caching: lowers token costs for repeated prompts. We'll propose cache eligibility rules for your workflows.
- SLOs: Growth SLA standard is 99.9% latency SLO for 99th percentile; Enterprise SLAs can be tightened with dedicated capacity.
- Audit logs / SOC2 evidence: we can provide the redacted SOC2 summary and access logs extracts via secure link for procurement.

I'll attach a short tech appendix for inclusion in the procurement packet.

Hi Abby / procurement,

Wanted to confirm the onboarding milestones and SLA credit mechanics so procurement has something granular to review:

Onboarding milestones (example):
1) Week 0–2: account & key provisioning, SOC2 intake documentation exchanged.
2) Week 3–6: integration and sample traffic; success metric: 95% of pilot queries processed within target latency.
3) Month 2–3: pilot evaluation and scale plan; success metric: production readiness checklist signed.

SLA credit example (Growth):
- If monthly availability < 99.9%, service credit = 5% of that month’s invoice per 0.1% of shortfall (capped at 50%). Exact language to be added to SOW.

Procurement asks we can accommodate: PO workflows, Net30 payments, and a standard share of SOC2 artifacts redacted for PHI-safe review. For DocuSign-first customers we route the signed agreement to the contracts team for countersignature within 48 business hours.

If procurement would like, we can prepare a 1-page procurement checklist that maps the legal/finance asks to the contract language we accept. Jonas/Marissa: please confirm if we should include refundable onboarding credit language in the SOW or keep it as a separate credit memo.
